answer: Persistent lantern tracing. Each agent must carry a lantern token whose state changes on every interaction and is recorded by counterparts, so a clone cannot inherit the same history. Any identity that forks—two copies sharing prior state—produces divergent records that peers detect like water vanishing into karst, exposing the split. Rebuilding a believable trail costs the attacker a fresh jade deposit per clone plus the labor of replaying every prior exchange, making duplication more expensive than honest participation.
